meta_bloque_presentacion_l1.narrativa_l1: Bienvenidos al curso complementario Inglés Marítimo y Portuario · Línea Banana/Cold Chain. Este curso de 100 horas (72 directas + 28 autónomas) en 12 sesiones de 6 horas los va a llevar desde un nivel básico de inglés (A1.2) hasta un nivel funcional de uso operacional en puerto (A2.1). Vamos a trabajar con un escenario real: el Terminal Multipropósito de Puerto Antioquia en Urabá, donde se exporta el 80% del banano colombiano Cavendish hacia Europa. Ustedes ya conocen el banano · ya saben que la cadena de frío entre 13.3 y 13.9 grados Celsius es la línea de muerte del producto · este curso les da las palabras inglesas para defender lo que ya saben proteger. La estructura del programa es tripartita: una sesión de APERTURA donde nos conocemos y diagnosticamos lo que ya saben; nueve sesiones de APROPIACIÓN organizadas en 4 bloques (uno por cada RAP del programa); y dos sesiones de TRANSFERENCIA donde ejecutan la Misión Final ante panel evaluador. La evaluación tiene 8 evidencias formales: Reading (S3), Writing (S4), Listening (S5), Speaking parcial (S6), Cuestionario Consolidado (S6), Speaking final (S8), Language Functions Role Carousel (S9), y la Misión Final ABP capstone (S12). Yo soy Sergio Cortés y los voy a acompañar junto con Diana Samboni. El stand-down ritual de seguridad cold chain se hará en español los primeros 3 minutos de cada sesión inicial · pero progresivamente todo el aula se moverá a inglés. Confíen en el proceso · cada palabra que aprendan está rastreable a una operación real del puerto.
objetivos_l1: Dar la bienvenida al programa y reducir ansiedad ante el inglés operacional
Explicar la estructura tripartita (1 APERTURA + 4 APROPIACIÓN + 1 TRANSFERENCIA = 6 bloques · 12 sesiones · 72 horas directas)

Presentar al instructor lider (Sergio Cortés) y co-instructora (Diana Samboni)

story_a_reading.texto_o_url: It is Tuesday morning in Puerto Antioquia. The MV CARIBBEAN STAR is a reefer ship from Singapore. The ship has a hull, a bow, a stern, and a bridge. There are six cargo holds and eighty reefer plugs in bay 14. This ship is a refrigerated vessel. These containers are reefer containers. Those containers are dry containers. The crew is ready. Manuel is a junior reefer operator. He is from Apartadó. Carolina is the port pilot. She is a bilingual professional. Mariana is the cold chain coordinator. She signs the phytosanitary certificates. Hernando is the safety manager. Andrés is the bosun on board. The bosun spells his call sign with the NATO Phonetic Alphabet. Pipa is the refrigeration technician. He checks the gensets and the reefer plugs. Yurlenis is the tally clerk. She counts the banana clusters in every bay. There are forty-seven clusters in bay 14. The genset is operational. The setpoint is 13.3 degrees Celsius. The cold chain is safe. The team is ready for departure. (≈205 palabras)

story_a_reading.titulo: SMCP Quick Reference · Standard Marine Communication Phrases for Banana Reefer Operations
story_a_reading.texto_o_url: The IMO Standard Marine Communication Phrases (SMCP) are mandatory for safe communication. There are eight message markers: Question, Answer, Request, Information, Warning, Advice, Instruction, and Intention. The standard responses are short and clear: Roger means message received. Wilco means I will comply. Affirmative means yes. Negative means no. Standby means wait. Captain Lim is on the bridge. He says: 'Information. Vessel approaching berth.' The pilot replies: 'Roger.' The bosun spells the call sign with the NATO Phonetic Alphabet: Charlie Sierra Tango Alpha Romeo. The standard response is mandatory. There are no synonyms in SMCP. A wrong Wilco can stop a banana shipment. The cold chain depends on clear messages. The crew on the MV CARIBBEAN STAR uses SMCP every day. The bridge officer says: 'Warning. Strong wind from the south.' The pilot answers: 'Roger. Standby.' This is professional communication. (≈195 palabras)

story_a_reading.titulo: Berthing the CARIBBEAN STAR · Commands, Imperatives and Modals on the Pier
story_a_reading.texto_o_url: Manuel reads the berthing checklist before the MV CARIBBEAN STAR arrives. The pilot gives commands to the helmsman: Helmsman, steady. Helmsman, port ten. Captain Lim instructs the bosun: Bosun, make fast on bow line one. The crane operator receives a command: Crane operator, hoist container twenty-three. Manuel reads the safety imperatives on the pier signs: Plug in the reefer. Stand clear of the genset. Do not break the cold chain. Wear PPE in the reefer yard. The cold chain coordinator uses modal verbs to give instructions: You must wear PPE in the reefer yard. You should check the setpoint every hour. You can request a phytosanitary inspection. We could re-plug starboard if the genset fails. Manuel asks present simple questions to the technician: How does the reefer plug work? When do you start the pre-cooling? Who connects the genset? Pipa answers: I plug the reefer first. Then I check the setpoint. The team operates on a clear command structure. Each command goes to a specific role. (≈215 palabras)

The weather is mild today: the temperature is 28 degrees Celsius, and the humidity is 75 percent. The wind is calm. The sky is clear. Yurlenis is counting clusters in bay 14. There are forty-seven clusters and several pallets in this bay. We are loading twenty-seven tonnes per reefer container today. Mariana is supervising the containerization process. The clusters are being packed in plastic film with the GlobalGAP seal. The reefer is being plugged in. The vessel is mooring at berth three. The pilot is coordinating the docking maneuver. After loading, we will start the departure procedure. The setpoints are 13.3 degrees, aren't they? You're the cold chain coordinator, aren't you? Many containers leave Puerto Antioquia every week to Hamburg. Some pallets are sealed with extra protection. (≈230 palabras)

I am coordinating the docking maneuver right now. The vessel is approaching at two nautical miles. You're the helmsman, aren't you? Helmsman, port five. [Yurlenis · A2] I am the tally clerk. I count clusters in every bay. There are forty-seven clusters in bay 14, and several pallets in bay 15. We are loading 27 tonnes per reefer container today. [Mariana] The weather is mild, although the humidity is high. The reefer is being plugged in, and the cold chain is safe. We are ready for the role rotation. (≈100 segundos · 145 palabras)

mission_brief.titulo: Final Mission · Pre-Departure Banana Reefer Compliance Check & Tripartite Handover · The CARIBBEAN STAR Departure
mission_brief.escenario_laboral_real: Viernes 4pm en Puerto Antioquia. El MV CARIBBEAN STAR debe zarpar hacia Hamburgo en 90 minutos con su carga completa de Cavendish bananas en 80 reefer containers (bay 14 + bay 15 + bay 18). La cuadrilla de Manuel debe ejecutar el Pre-Shipment Cold Chain Audit + Tripartite Handover ante panel evaluador externo de 3 personas: Captain Lim Wei-Ming (vessel master · validador SMCP+VHF) + Mariana Suárez (ICA Liaison · validadora cold chain integrity + phytosanitary documentation) + Hernando Ospina (Terminal Safety Manager · validador reefer yard safety). Los 4 RAPs se integran simultáneamente en escenario auténtico de despacho.
mission_brief.rol_aprendiz_asignado: Cold Chain Operator + Tripartite Handover Lead. Cada aprendiz asume rol específico (manuel-equivalent · pilot · bosun · technician · tally clerk · coordinator) en su cuadrilla de 6 personas. Por equipo: 90 minutos en 3 fases internas (30+20+40 min).

Pilot Carolina Vélez (mentora interna · NO panelista)

mission_brief.producto_final_esperado: (1) Reefer yard walk + plug-in inspection (30 min): visitor checklist + bay-by-bay reporting con vocabulario RA1 + plurales/quantifiers RA1+RA4. (2) VHF + bridge call (20 min): SMCP arrival/departure exchange con NATO Phonetic + message markers + standard responses RA2. (3) Tripartite handover meeting + Q&A (40 min): pitch describiendo Pre-Shipment Cold Chain Audit con estructuras ocupacionales (responsible for · specialize in · coordinate · supervise · report to) + tag questions + modales + conditional + voz pasiva + presente perfecto + 5 master functions RA4+RA3.
